body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so compliance counts are weighed with caution. I favour portfolios the CIO can build from that meet the 8-12% volatility band, or come close to it, and that rely on covariance structure over return forecasts, in line with the late-cycle finding. First is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, 13.3 effective assets, a 0.63 backtest Sharpe and a 0.44 CRO risk score. It addresses the estimation-error weakness that reviewers found in my own concentrated 46% us_value position. Its reviewers flagged only the premise of unbiased CMA noise and the gamma tuning, and neither is fatal. Second is pc_researcher. It has the highest ex-ante Sharpe among the others (0.51), a 0.70 backtest Sharpe, a -10.9% drawdown and only two breaches (volatility and tracking error). Its reviewers raised the Sharpe-above-ceiling inconsistency and the unimposed volatility floor, so I rank it below the compliant option. Third is black_litterman. It is compliant with a 0.70 backtest Sharpe and moderate 3.01% tracking error. The gamma wording inconsistency is a real flaw, but it is a documentation error and does not undermine the weights. Fourth is cvar_minimization. It is compliant, has a 0.74 backtest Sharpe, and its reviewers found the method correctly applied. Its weaknesses are noisy tail estimates and a concentrated 2.9 effective N. Fifth is tail_risk_parity. It is a forecast-free, covariance-based diversifier with a 0.29 CRO risk score, and it adds family diversity to the ensemble. It sits well below the 8% volatility floor and has three breaches. Even so, its 0.39 Sharpe and -7.2% drawdown make it more useful than the other defensive options. Why first beats fifth: resampled_efficient_frontier is compliant, broad, and carries 7.11% return at the band floor, while tail_risk_parity breaches return, volatility and tracking error and cannot serve as a standalone base. For the flag I choose hierarchical_risk_parity. It holds 91.9% cash, 1.4 effective assets and 0.14 Sharpe, and it has three breaches. Its own reviews call it a mandate failure that reflects the method working on a degenerate cash input, so the CIO should not lean on it.
